data: この 大学[だいがく]の 図書[としょ]館[かん]には、 アジア 経済[けいざい]に 関[かん]する 本[ほん]が たくさん あります。
There are many books related to the economy of Asia in this university's library.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 に関する N2 formal "with regard to; concerning; regarding; about; on; related to"
私[わたし]が 今[こん]学期[がっき] 取[と]っている 授業[じゅぎょう]の うちで、 宿題[しゅくだい]が ないのは タンスの クラスだけだ。
Out of the classes I'm taking this semester, the only one with no homework is dance.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のうち(で) "in; of; among" Xのうち(で）is used to indicate the total entity (X) when presenting a part or portion of X.
今年[ことし]は 12[じゅうに]月[がつ]に なっても なかなか 寒[さむ]くならない。 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の せいだろうか。
This year it just hasn't gotten cold even though it's already December. I wonder if it's because of global warming.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
明日[あした]に なっても 犬[いぬ]が 見付[みつ]からない 場合[ばあい]は、 ペット レスキュー センターに 探[さが]しに 行[い]きましょう。
In case we don't find the dog tomorrow, let's go look for it at the pet rescue center.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
A: あれっ、 その 足[あし]、 どう したの。 B: 実[じつ]は さあ、 昨日[きのう]、 階段[かいだん]で 転[ころ]んじゃってさあ、 骨[ほね]、 折[お]っちゃったんだよ。
A: Oh, what did you do to your leg? B: Actually, I fell down some stairs yesterday and ended up breaking it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

phrase/clause/sentence さ(あ) "(you know)" さ occurs after phrases, clauses, or sentences in very casual conversation. One function is to catch the hearer's attention, but it is also used as a filler with no meaning.
日本[にほん]の 若[わか]い 人[ひと]たちと 友達[ともだち]に なりたかったら、 「です・ます」の 話[はな]し方[かた]の 代[か]わりに、 カジュアルな 話[はな]し方[かた]で 話[はな]した ほうが いいよ。
If you want to make friends with young Japanese, you should use casual speech instead of the desu/masu form.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: の代わりに is used to present something/someone that is replacing or has replaced something/someone. When the context is clear, Noun の can be omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in place of; instead of; to make up for --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nの代わりに
技術[ぎじゅつ]の 進歩[しんぽ]に つれて、 私[わたし]達[たち]の 生活[せいかつ]は 便利[べんり]になった。
As technology advances, our lives have become more convenient.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nにつれて "as ~; with ~" Xにつれて indicates that omething takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-V.
物[もの] 言[い]わぬ 自然[しぜん]に 代[だい]割[わり]って、 自然[しぜん]の 大切[たいせつ]さを 話[はな]したいと 思[おも]う。
Since nature doesn't speak, I would like to speak on its behalf about its importance.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-nai ぬ "not" ぬ is a verb ending from classical Japanese and is equivalent to ない in meaning and form. In modern Japanese, it often appears in set phrases.
台風[たいふう]が 近[ちか]いづいている ため、 九州[きゅうしゅう]を 中心[ちゅうしん]に 大雨[おおあめ]が 降[ふ]っている。
Due to the approaching typhoon, heavy rain is falling, centered in Kyushu.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N を 中心 {と/に} (して） "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." Nを中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify verbs. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
「電気[でんき]の 町[まち]」 秋葉原[あきはばら]は、 最近[さいきん] 「お宅[たく]の 町[まち]」だとも 言[い]われている。
Akihabara is said to be "Electronics Town", but now it is said that it's "Otaku Town"
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
子供[こども]同士[どうし]の けんかが 原因[げんいん]で、 親[おや]同士[どうし]の 関係[かんけい]も 悪[わる]くなってしまった。
A fight between the children also caused the relationship between the two sets of parents to sour.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
日本[にほん]での インターンシップの 経験[けいけん]は、 私[わたし]の 人生[じんせい]を 大[おお]きく 左右[さゆう] するだろう。
My internship experience in Japan will probably have a big impact on my life.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を N2 左右する "influence; govern" 左右する is most commonly used in written language.
ハワイは １[いち]年[ねん] 中気[ちゅうき]温[おん]が 高[たか]いけれど、 高[たか]い 山[やま]では 雪[ゆき]が 降[ふ]る 事[こと]も 有[あ]る そうだ。
Hawaii is warm all year around, but I hear that there are times when it snows in the high mountains.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain-nonpast ことがある is used when something occurs (or someone does something) occasionally. も implies that something else may also occur. Note: This phrase should not be confused with V-plain-PAST ことがある (e.g. 日本に行ったことがある。) which states previous experience. --- 英訳 [English translation]: There are times when ~, sometimes --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain-nonpast こと{が / も}ある
日本[にほん]語[ご]では、 目上[めうえ]の 人[ひと]に 対[たい]して 「あなた」と 呼[よ]ぶのは とても 失礼[しつれい]な ことだ。
In Japanese, it's very rude to address your superiors as "anata".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に対して "toward; for; in; with regard to" This grammar marks something to/toward/about which one does something, or mark someone to/toward whom one does something or owes something. In different contexts, it can mark something one has interest in. Do not confuse with the use where に対して indicates two contrasting actions, states, situations, etc.
北海道[ほっかいどう]の ホスト ファミリーの お母[かあ]さんは 元気[げんき]かなあ。 今晩[こんばん]、 電話[でんわ] してみよう。
I wonder how my host mom in Hokkaido is. I'll give her a call tonight.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 〜かなあ is a sentence final particle which indicates that the sentence is a self-addressed question or a question addressed to the speaker's in-group member(s). It is used only in casual language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I wonder ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜かな(あ)
日本[にほん] 経済[けいざい] 新聞[しんぶん]や ウォール ストリート ジャーナルには、 ビジネス向[む]けの 記事[きじ]が 多[おお]い。
In papers like Nihon Keizai Shinbun and the Wall Street Journal, many articles are written with businessmen in mind.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N 向けの N2. Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.
子供[こども]の 時[とき]から 長[なが]い 間[あいだ] 練習[れんしゅう] し続[つづ]けて、 とうとう オリンピックに 参加[さんか] する ことが できた。
I've been practicing ever since I was a child, and now at last I'm getting to compete in the Olympics.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

とうとう V "finally; at (long) last; eventually; in the end; after all" とうとう indicates that an expected situation has occurred after an extended period of time. The adverb ついに is similar to とうとう and can be used in the place of とうとう. ついに is more formal.
土[つち]の 中[なか]から 魚[さかな]の 骨[ほね]や 貝[かい]などが 出[で]てきた ことから、 ここは 大昔[おおむかし] 海[うみ]だったと いう ことが 分[わ]かった。
Based on the fact that fish bones and shells were unearthed here, we've learned that long ago this place used to be under the sea.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ことから "because; from the fact that" ことから is used to express a reason
1980[せんきゅうひゃくはちじゅう]年[ねん] 代[だい]の 後半[こうはん]から 1990[せんきゅうひゃくきゅうじゅう]年[ねん] 代[だい]の 初[はじ]めに かけての 日本[にほん]の 経済[けいざい]は 「バブル 経済[けいざい]」と 呼[よ]ばれている。
Japan's economy from the latter half of the 1980s through the beginning of the 1990s is referred to as a "bubbly economy".
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
1900/1910/1920/etc. + 年代 "1990s/1910s/1920s/etc." the suffix 代 is used with 10 or its multiples and 年 to refer to a certain decade.
A) 今日[きょう]、 田中[たなか]さん、 クラス 休[やす]んだ。 B） そう 言[い]えば、 昨日[きのう]、 おなかが 痛[いた]いって 言[い]ってたよ。 病気[びょうき]かも しれないね。
A) Tanaka missed class today, didn't she? B) Come to think of it, yesterday she said that her stomach hurt. She might be sick.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
そう言えば Means: That reminds me; Now i remember; indeed This conjunctive phrase is used when the speaker is reminded of something by the hearer's remark or the speaker's own remark.
日本[にほん]の 名所[めいしょ]と 言[い]えば、 温泉[おんせん]も 忘[わす]れる 事[こと]は 出来[でき]ません。
Speaking of "famous places of Japan," you can't forget about onsens.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ~と言えば, which literally means "if you say that--," is used to present, as the topic, something or someone that has just been mentioned by the hearer or speaker. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ X と言えば (X is usually a noun phrase)
日本[にほん]語[ご]は 文法[ぶんぽう]が 難[むずか]しいのに 対[たい]して、 中国[ちゅうごく]語[ご]は 発音[はつおん]が 難[むずか]しい。
Whereas the difficult part of Japanese is its grammar, the difficult part of Chinese is its pronunciation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Sのに対して "whereas; on the other hand; in contrast" に対して is used when contrasting two actions, states, situations, etc.
将来[しょうらい]は、 自分[じぶん]の 能力[のうりょく]を 生[い]かす ことが 出来[でき]る 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]きたい。
In the future, I want to work at a company that puts my skills to good use.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
両親[りょうしん]が 亡[な]くなった 後[あと]、 私[わたし]は 兄[あに]と ともに 二人[ふたり]で 助[たす]け合[あ]って 生[い]きてきました。
Since my parents died, my older brother and I have helped each other (and managed) to get by.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nと共に "with; along with; as" indicates that someone does something or that something happens with N.
子供[こども]向[む]けに 作[つく]られた 映画[えいが]の 中[なか]にも、 大人[おとな]が 見[み]ても 楽[たの]しい ものが たくさん ある。
There are lots of films that, although made for children, are still enjoyable for adults to watch.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N 向けに V Means: for; made for; for the use of; directed to The suffix 向け adds the meaning "made for; for the use of; directed toward." 向け is often affixed to nouns which refer to people, countries and organizations.
この 大学[だいがく]では、 日本[にほん]語[ご]、 あるいは、 英語[えいご]で 卒業[そつぎょう] 論文[ろんぶん]を 書[か]く ことに なっている。
At this university, senior theses are expected to be written in either Japanese or English.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
毎晩[まいばん] コーラス 部[ぶ]の 練習[れんしゅう]が 有[あ]るので、 勉強[べんきょう]を し始[はじ]めるのは いつも １０[じゅう]時[じ]過[す]ぎだ。
Because I have practice at chorus club every night, I always start studying after 10:00.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: 始める in this use is an auxiliary verb meaning "begin to V." --- 英訳 [English translation]: begin to, begin-V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Verb-masu 始める
コンビニには、 生活[せいかつ] 用品[ようひん]でも 食[た]べ物[もの]でも 雑誌[ざっし]や 新聞[しんぶん]でも、 なんでも 置[お]いてある。
They've got everything at convenience stores, from everyday essentials to food to magazines and newspapers.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 でも N2 でも "including X and Y; whether (it is) X or Y" This is used to provide examples for the statement in the sentence. This structure implies that there are also things other than the examples which make the statement true. Note that XもYも (both X and Y) does not carry such an implication..
トムさんは 昨日[きのう] よく 勉強[べんきょう] していたから、 今日[きょう]の 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 試験[しけん]、 簡単[かんたん]だったでしょ。
Tom, you studied hard last night, so I guess your Japanese test today was easy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
子供[こども]の 時[とき]、 アニメが 大好[だいす]きだったんだ。 それで、 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] しようと 思[おも]ったんだ。
When I was a child I loved anime. Because of that I thought I would study Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: It is a sentence-initial conjunction. It precedes a fact, conclusion, decision, etc. S1 is the cause/reason for the information stated in S2. それで cannot be used when S2 is the speaker's judgement, request or command. In this situation, だから should be used. Note that だから can be used in situations where それで is used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because of that; so; that's why; for that reason --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。それで、S２。
日本[にほん]と 私[わたし]の 国[くに]は、 朝[あさ]と 夜[よる]が 逆[ぎゃく]だ。 いま、 こちらは 午後[ごご] ９[く]時[じ]だが、 日本[にほん]は 午前[ごぜん] １０[じゅう]時[じ]だ。
The mornings and evenings in my country are opposite that of Japan. Here it is 9PM, but in Japan it is 10AM.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

X は 逆 だ。 "be opposite; the other way" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
一方[いっぽう] 通行[つうこう]の 道[みち]だと いう ことを 知[し]らないで、 逆[ぎゃく]の 方向[ほうこう]に 進[すす]んでしまい、 警察[けいさつ]に つかまってしまった。
I went against traffic, not realizing it was a one-way street, and ended up getting pulled over by the police.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

逆 の N。 "opposite N; the reverse of N" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
将来[しょうらい]、 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]きたいと 思[おも]っている。 その ためには もっと 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]にならなくては いけない。
In the future, I want to work at a Japanese company. For that purpose, I need to become more skilled at Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
最近[さいきん]、 若[わか]い 人[ひと]の 間[あいだ]で 言葉[ことば]の 使[つか]い方[かた]に 変化[へんか]が 見[み]られる。
You can see changes recently in the way young people are using language.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 見られる is the passive form of 見る and means "be observed." 見られる can also be interpreted as the potential form of 見る, in which case it means "can observe/see" --- 英訳 [English translation]: (something) is observed; (one) can observe/see --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nが見られる
私[わたし]の 知[し]っている 限[かぎ]り、 外国[がいこく]人[じん]が 使[つか]いやすい 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 辞書[じしょ]は ないんですよ。
As far as I know, there's no Japanese dictionary that's easy for non-native speakers to use.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
日曜[にちよう] 日[び]の ピクニックは お天気[てんき] 次第[しだい]ですよ。 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]れば 来週[らいしゅう]に 延期[えんき] される そうです。
The picnic this Sunday is dependant on the weather. I heard that if it rains, it'll be postboned until next week.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N次第だ "depend on N" When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
地球[ちきゅう]の 未来[みらい]を 考[かんが]えた とき、 何[なに]よりも まず 初[はじ]めに 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]が 問題[もんだい]に されるべきだ。
When thinking about the future of the Earth, global warming is the issue that must be addressed before anything else.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N/NP が問題に {される／なる} "X becomes an issue; X is brought up as an issue; X is questioned; X is called into question." X を 問題にする means "to bring X up as an issue" or "to question X." This phrase is often used in the passive form Xが問題にされる. Xが問題になる is also common. The meaning is the same as that of the passive version.
大学[だいがく]に 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]だって 言[い]っても、 家賃[やちん]が 高[たか]すぎるから、 この 部屋[へや]は 借[か]りられない。
Even if its location is close to the university, the rent for this room is too high for me to rent it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain {と/って} 言っても "although ~ say/said that ~; even though ~ say/said that ~" Its used to clarify what has just been said in order to avoid misunderstanding. って is used in place of と in casual conversation or writing.
将来[しょうらい]、 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]の 先生[せんせい]に なりたいと 思[おも]っています。 そこで、 ボランティアで 子供[こども]達[たち]を 教[おし]えてみる ことに しました。
I'm thinking that I want to become an elementary school teacher in the future, so I've decided to try teaching children on a volunteer basis.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1, そこで, S2. "Because of that; therefore; so" そこで is used to indicate and action (to be) taken because of the situation presented in S1. それで may replace そこで そこで may only replace それで when S2 is a controllable action. ex. 寒かった。それで、見に来た人が少なかった。 only それで can be used here.
A: スミスさんは、 将来[しょうらい] 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]くのが 夢[ゆめ]なんだって。 B: へー、 スミスさんが そんな 夢[ゆめ]を 持[も]っているなんて、 絶対[ぜったい] 知[し]らなかった。
A: They say Ms. Smith's dream is to work at a Japanese company in the future. B: Really? I had no idea she had a dream like that.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.
九州[きゅうしゅう]か 四国[しこく]へ 行[い]く。 本[ほん]か 雑誌[ざっし]が ある。 友達[ともだち]か 家族[かぞく]と 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]く。
I will go either to kyushu or shikoku. There are either books or magazines. I will go travel with either my friends or family.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The phrase AかBか is used to present alternatives. When Bか is followed by a case particle (e.g., が, を, へ, に, で, と), the second か is usually dropped. --- 英訳 [English translation]: either A or B; whether A or B --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. 〜か〜か b. N1かN2+Particle
私[わたし]は、 最近[さいきん]、 日本[にほん]の 若者[わかもの] 言語[げんご]を 中心[ちゅうしん]と した 言語[げんご]の 研究[けんきゅう]を しています。
Lately, I am making the language of young Japanese people the focus of my language research.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1を中心(と/に)した N2 (= N1中心のN2) "(centering) around; focusing on; mainly; with N as the center/focus/leader/etc." N1を中心(と/に)する literally means "to make N the center." This phrase takes 2 forms. The form used here is used to modify nouns. The phrase indicates that something takes place around N or with N as the center/focus, or that someone does something focusing on N.
せっかく 4[よん]年間[ねんかん]も 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] したのに、 大学[だいがく]を 卒業[そつぎょう] してから あまり 使[つか]わなかったら、 だんだん 忘[わす]れてしまった。
I put in four whole years studying Japanese, but I haven't used it much since I graduated from the university, so now bit by bit I'm forgetting it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
父[ちち]は １０[じゅう]年[ねん] 前[まえ]に 亡[な]くなった。 それ 以来[いらい]、 母[はは]は 一人[ひとり]で 私[わたし]達[たち] 兄弟[きょうだい]を 育[そだ]ててくれた。
My father passed away ten years ago. Since then, my mother has reared my brother and me on her own.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
VN/Nいらい "since ~" It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
道後[どうご] 温泉[おんせん]は 日本[にほん]の 一番[いちばん] 古[ふる]い 温泉[おんせん]で、 ３０００[さんぜん]年[ねん]の 歴史[れきし]が 有[あ]ると 言[い]われています。
It is said that the Dougo Onsen, with 3000 years of history, is the oldest onsen in Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to introduce something commonly said about something or someone. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~ it is said to be ~, It is said that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ーはSentence-plainと言われている
この カレーは 涙[なみだ]が できるほど 辛[つら]い。
This curry is so spicy it brings tears to your eyes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
疲[つか]れていて 話[はなし]も できないほどだった。
We were so tired we couldn't even speak.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
この カレーは 辛[つら]すぎて、 まったく 食[た]べられない。
This curry is so hot that I can't eat even a bite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく〜ない "not ~ at all; not ~ in the least" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
この カレーは かなり 辛[つら]いけれど、 食[た]べられない ことは ない。
This curry is pretty spicy, but not to the extent that I can't eat it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
疲[つか]れていたので、 テレビを つけっぱなしにして 寝[ね]てしまった。
I was tired, so I fell asleep without turning off the TV.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masuっぱなしにする "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
ウェイターに デザート メニューを 持[も]ってきてくれる ように 頼[たの]もうか。
Shall we ask the waiter to bring us the dessert menu?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
彼[かれ]、 上手（なん）[じょうず]だっけ。?
Is he skillful?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANa/N/QW} (なん）だっけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
この 岩[いわ]を 磨[みが]き上[あ]げてください。
Please polish up this rock.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

磨き上げる (V-masu 上げる） transitive "to polish up; to shine up" Affixed to the masu-stems of verbs, 上げる forms compound verbs, adding meanings such as "finish something up," "upward" or "to a great extent." the meaning is determined by the preceding verb.
彼[かれ]、 上手[じょうず]じゃなかった （んだ）っけ?
Is he not skillful?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{ANA/N} じゃなかった（んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
この カレーは 辛[つら]くて 涙[なみだ]が 出[で]るほどだ。
This curry is so spicy it brings tears to your eyes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
デートを し始[はじ]めて、 彼[かれ]の ことが ますます 好[す]きになった。
I've come to like him even more since we started dating.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ますます Adv "more and more; -er and -er; increasingly; even more; even -er; still more; still -er" ますます occurs with verbs, the adverbial forms of adjectives and adverbs. It indicates that something happens to an even greater (or lesser) degree than before. ますます is NOT used for future controllable events. For example, it cannot replace もっともっと in もっともっとがんばって下さい。
寝[ね]られなくなるので、 私[わたし]は ほとんど コーヒーは 飲[の]まない。
It keeps me from sleeping, so I almost never drink coffee.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんどの N means Almost all N; most of N
環境[かんきょう]の ために、 紙[かみ]を リサイクル する ようにしてください。
For the sake of the environment, please try to recycle paper.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Here one makes an effort at every opportunity to do something to the degree that he or she can, but sometimes fails. Thus ようにする is often used for habitual actions. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
彼[かれ]は、 デートの たびに おいしい レストランに 連[つ]れて行[い]ってくれる。
He takes me to a good restaurant every time we go out on a date.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Nのたびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
ダイエットを しているから、 甘[あま]い 物[もの]は なるべく 食[た]べない ようにしています。
I'm on diet, so I'm trying to eat as few sweets as I can.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なるべく with or without an adverb modifies the following verb phrase and adds the meaning "as (much) as possible." When there is no specific adverb after なるべく, it is usually interpreted as "as much as~" or "as often as~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: as much/often as possible; as ~ as possible --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ なるべく
メールが 戻[もど]って来[き]たと いう ことは、 この アドレスは もう 使[つか]われていないと いう ことに なる。
The mail came back, so that means this address is no longer being used.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S(という)ことになる Means: end up (with); mean that ~; cause This grammar is usually preceded by 1 of 3 types of sentences, here is is (1) a topic phrase, and indicates that the (non-) action, even or situation stated in the preceding phrase/clause leads to a logical conclusion or a certain situation.
性格[せいかく]は 人[ひと]に よって 違[ちが]います。
Character/personality differs depending on the person.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
生[う]み出[だ]す 見[み]つけ出[だ]す 掘[ほ]り出[だ]す
うみだす - to create みつけだすー to find out ほりだす- to dig up/out
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. V-masu 出す has 2 meanings, here is the (1) Someone makes something available/accessible which hasn't existed or hasn't been available or accessible.
彼[かれ]と 私[わたし]の 考[かんが]えは まったく 同[おな]じだ。
His idea and mine are exactly the same.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく {V/A/ANo/(の)N/Ano} "totally; utterly; entirely; completely; extremely; absolutely; really" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
日本[にほん]に 引[ひ]っ越[こ]す ことに なりました。
It was decided (by someone else) that I must move to Japan.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-non-pastことになった means that a situation has changed due to some external force (e.g. a decision made by someone other than the speaker). It indicates either that the speaker (or the subject of the sentence) did not actively make the decision or that he/she is viewing the decision from the standpoint of an outsider. Note that ことにした indicates that the speaker or the subject made a decision to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It was/has been decided that ~; It turns out that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-non-past.plain-ことになった:{行く/行かない}ことになった
あの 小娘[こむすめ]は、 まるで 子猫[こねこ]の ようだ。
That young girl is just like a kitten.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Sentence ending form: 〜ようだ。 "as if ~ (were/-ed); just like" This structure is used to introduce a simile, i.e., to describe a thing, person, action, etc. by comparing it with a similar thing, person, action, etc. まるで is an emphatic marker.
熱[あつ]い うちに、 どうぞ 召[め]し上[あ]がって下[くだ]さい。
While it is still hot, please eat. (very polite phrasing)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (ない)うちに is used when someone does something before a situation or state changes. 間に is used in similar situations, but it cannot be used with the negative forms of verbs. Another difference between the two phrases is that うちに always implies that it is not possible, easy or a good idea to do something after the time specified by the うちに clause. However, this is not always the case with 間に. Thus far, if it is not a problem for the speaker to go to Japan after finishing his Japanese class, 間に should be used, as shown below: 日本語の勉強をしている間に日本に行ってみたい。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: while ~ still ～ないうちに＝ before (something happens) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ～うちに
原爆[げんばく]の 恐[おそ]ろしさは いまだに 忘[わす]れる ことが できない。
I still can't forget the horrors of the atomic bomb.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
何[なん]だ、 もう 食[た]べちゃったの。 一緒[いっしょ]に 食[た]べたかったのに。
Wait, you already ate? But I wanted to eat together.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
なんだ "oh!" The literal meaning of なんだ is "What is X?" However it can also be used to express the speaker's slight surprise。 Used only in very casual conversation.
コンサートが なかなか 始[はじ]まらないので、 客[きゃく]が 怒[おこ]り出[だ]した。
The concert is taking forever to begin, so the audience has started to get angry.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
A： 頭[あたま]が 痛[いた]いです。 B： それなら、 すぐに 寝[ね]た 方[ほう]が いいよ。
A: My head aches. B: If that's the case, you should go to bed right away.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
それなら "If that's the case; If so" それ meaning "that" refers to the speaker's previous statement of the statement which was just made by the hearer.
彼[かれ]と 別[わか]れても がっかり する こと ないよ。 もっと いい 人[ひと]が すぐ 見[み]つかるから。
You don't have to be down just because you broke up with your boyfriend. You'll meet someone much better in no time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past すること（は）ない "don't have to ~; don't need to ~; It's not necessary to ~; There is no need to ~" In casual conversation the は may drop.
環境[かんきょう]を よく する ため、 来月[らいげつ]から リサイクル キャンペーンを する ことに なった。
In an effort to improve the environment, it's been decided that as of next month we'll begin a recycling campaign.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-non-pastことになった means that a situation has changed due to some external force (e.g. a decision made by someone other than the speaker). It indicates either that the speaker (or the subject of the sentence) did not actively make the decision or that he/she is viewing the decision from the standpoint of an outsider. Note that ことにした indicates that the speaker or the subject made a decision to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It was/has been decided that ~; It turns out that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-non-past.plain-ことになった:{行く/行かない}ことになった
なぜ 彼[かれ]は 私[わたし]の ことを 愛[あい]してくれないのだろうか。 私[わたし]は 彼[かれ]が こんなに 好[す]きなのに。
Why doesn't he love me back when I love him so much?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Sの（だろう／でしょう）か Means: I wonder ~ Indicates a self-addressed question which can either be a yes-no question or a wh- question.
疲[つか]れていたので、 電気[でんき]を つけた まま 寝[ね]てしまった。 ネクタイも した ままだった。
I was tired, so I fell asleep with the lights still on. I left my tie on, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Aまま（で）V "V with ~; V while ~; V as (it is); V without ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
コーヒーには たくさん カフェインが 入[はい]っている。 したがって、 飲[の]み過[す]ぎると 寝[ね]られなくなる。
There's a lot of caffeine in coffee. Because of this, if you drink too much you won't be able to sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1 (reason/cause). したがって、S２ (consequence.) "therefore; accordingly; consequently; as a result; so"
バレンタインデーに チョコレートを くれたと いう ことは、 彼女[かのじょ]は 君[きみ]が 好[す]きだと いう ことなんだよ。
To be given chocolate on Valentine's Day means that a girl likes you.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate what X is or what X means. なのだ makes the statement more emphatic. To make this expression more formal, use である in place of だ. Also notice how the なの became なん in this example. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is Y; X means that Y --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ XはY(という)ことなの{である/だ} : 日本人のことなのである。
同[おな]じ 漢字[かんじ] また 間違[まちが]えた。
I got the same kanji wrong again.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
１８[じゅうはっ]歳[さい] 以上[いじょう]の 人[ひと]しか 見[み]られません。
Those who aren't 18 years old or more can't watch.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: X以上 and X以下 means "equal to or more than X" and "(equal to or) less than X," respectively. A Number + Counter or a demonstrative pronoun such as これ and それ commonly occurs before 以上 and 以下. When the topic is academic grades, grade symbols such as C and B can be used (e.g., C以上). --- 英訳 [English translation]: 以上 = or more 以下 = less than; or less --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) 以上/以下: ３年生以上 b. Demonstrative pronoun 以上/以下: これ以上; それ以下
明日[あした]の コンサート、 一緒[いっしょ]に 行[い]くだろう。
You're going with me to the concert tomorrow, right?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
私[わたし]たちは 話[はなし]も 出来[でき]ないほど 疲[つか]れていた。
We were so tired we couldn't even speak.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
腹[はら]の 立[た]つ ことには、 私[わたし]、 彼[かれ]が 好[す]きです。
What makes me angry is that I like him.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V.plain ことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
忙[いそが]し過[す]ぎて、 寝[ね]る 時間[じかん]さえ ありません。
I'm so busy I don't even have time to sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
もし 文法[ぶんぽう]が 間違[まちが]ってたら、 直[なお]してくれる？
If you find mistakes with the grammar, will you fix them for me?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
せっかくですが、 今日[きょう]は 仕事[しごと]が 忙[いそが]しくて。
This is a rare (event, invitation, etc), but I'm busy with work today...
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

せっかく{ですが／ですけど／だけど／etc} "with effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~; ~, which is a rare occasion/event/etc." せっかく is used in 2 situations: (2) when a given opportunity is rare and therefore he/she wants to make use of it; or, in spite of their opportunity, he/she cannot make use of it
国民[こくみん]は みんな 税金[ぜいきん]を 払[はら]わなければなりません。
All citizens have to pay taxes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
彼[かれ]は 彼女[かのじょ]と 結婚[けっこん] するべきでは なかったと 思[おも]う。
I think he never should have married her.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V. plain.non-past.aff べき {だ／じゃない／ではない／だった／じゃなかった／ではなかった} "should; ought to" The auxillary べき expresses the speaker's strong judgment that one should do something. The form of する before べき can be either す or する, as in すべき or するべき。
私[わたし]は 友達[ともだち]に ノートを 見[み]せてくれる ように 頼[たの]みました。
I asked my friend if he would let me see his notes. (Indirect Quote)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
さて、 もう 遅[おそ]いですだら、 今日[きょう]は これで 失礼[しつれい] します。
Well, its already late, so I'm going to excuse myself for today.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

(S1.) さて、S2. "well; now; well now" さて always occurs at the beginning of a sentence and signals that (a) the speaker/writer is beginning a new topic (the new topic and the previous topic may be part of the same discourse) (b) the speaker/writer is going to ask a question about the information just provided, or (c) the speaker is leaving. AS SEEN HERE さてis not used in casual situations.
昨日[きのう]は 疲[つか]れていたから、 1[いち]日[にち]中[ちゅう] ほとんど 寝[ね]ていました。
I was tired yesterday, so I slept almost all day long.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんど V Means "almost all; most of (it, the time, etc.)" It is only used with the amount of something is the issue.
暖[あたた]かくなるに つれて、 雪[ゆき]が 溶[と]け、 木[き]が 緑[みどり]に なっていく。
As it becomes warmer, the snow is melting and the trees are turning green.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-non-past.aff につれて "as ~; with ~" Xにつれて indicates that omething takes place as X occurs. X can be either a verb or the stem of a suru-V.
体[からだ]に 悪[わる]いから、 煙草[たばこ]は 吸[す]わない ようにした ほうが いいよ。
It's bad for you, so you should try not to smoke.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Here one makes an effort at every opportunity to do something to the degree that he or she can, but sometimes fails. Thus ようにする is often used for habitual actions. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
あの 仕事[しごと]は、 立[た]ちっぱなしの 仕事[しごと]だから、 疲[つか]れるに 違[ちが]い ない。
You don't get to sit down at that job, so it'll definitely tire you out.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu っぱなしの N "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
あの 喫茶[きっさ]店[てん]では コーヒーが たったの 200[にひゃく]円[えん]で 飲[の]める そうだ。
I heard that you can get coffee for just 200 yen at that coffee shop.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
どんなに 忙[いそが]しくても、 少[すく]なくとも 6[ろく]時間[じかん] はねた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
No matter how busy you are, you should get at least 6 hours of sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
少なくとも Number (+Counter) 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number (optionally followed by a counter). When は follows a number (+counter), it emphasizes the number.
一人[ひとり]の 人[ひと]しか 言[い]わない ことを 一般[いっぱん]化[か] するのは、 よく ありませんよ。
It's not a good idea to make a generalization based on what just one person has said, you know.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix 化[か] is affixed to nouns and no-adjectives and adds the meaning of "-ization," as in "mechanization" and "digitization." --- 英訳 [English translation]: ～化する = ize; make; become; change to ～化する = ization; making ~; becoming ~; changing to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 化: 日本化; 専門化; 機械化 (mechanization); カタカナ化 b. NO-Adj + 化: 最適化 (optimization)
バスが なかなか 来[こ]ない。 授業[じゅぎょう]に 遅[おく]れてしまい そうだ。 困[こま]ったなあ。
The bus just won't come. It looks like I'll be late for class. What should I do?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
妹[いもうと]は 怖[こわ]くて 夜[よる] 眠[ねむ]れなくなる くせに、 ホラー ムービーばかり 見[み]ている。
Even though she gets scared and can't sleep, my little sister always watches horror films.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜くせに Means: Although~; in spite of the fact that~; and yet~ This conjunction is used when something commonly expected from information in the subordinate clause (i.e. the くせに phrase/clause) does not happen or is not the case. In most situations, くせに expresses the speaker's anger, frustration or disagreement. This emotion is not directed toward the speaker, but toward the hearer or 3rd person. When くせに is used, the subject of the main clause and that of the subordinate clause must be the same. If the subjects differ, you must use なのに、.
お湯[ゆ]を わかしっぱなしで 忘[わす]れて 寝[ね]てしまい、 家事[かじ]に なり そうになった。
I almost started a fire when I forgot about the kettle I had put on and fell asleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu っぱなしだ／で "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
家賃[やちん]が 上[あ]がったので、 引[ひ]っ越[こ]さなければならない ことに なってしまった。
The rent went up, which means that I have to move.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S(という)ことになる Means: end up (with); mean that ~; cause This grammar is usually preceded by 1 of 3 types of sentences, here is is (2) reason clause, and indicates that the (non-) action, even or situation stated in the preceding phrase/clause leads to a logical conclusion or a certain situation.
あの アパートには 大学[だいがく]生[せい]が たくさん 住[す]んでいるから、 うるさいに 違[ちが]い ない。
There are a lot of college students living in that apartment, so it must be noisy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure indicates that the speaker is certain that something is true or is the case. It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない
この 猫[ねこ]、 拾[ひろ]ってきた ときは 死[し]に そうだったけど、 だんだん 元気[げんき]になったんだ。
When I took in this abandoned cat, it was close to dying, but little by little it's gotten healthier.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
彼[かれ]は 決[けっ]して 悪[わる]い 人間[にんげん]では ない。 ちょっと わがままな (selfish)だけだ。
He's not a bad person by any measure; he's just a little selfish.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
決して{ANa/ANo/N} {では/じゃ} { ない／なかった／ありません／ありませんでした}
引[ひ]っ越[こ]す 前[まえ]は、 アパートの 前[まえ]の 道[みち]が こんなに うるさい ことに 気[き]が つかなかった。
Before I moved in, I didn't realize that the street in front of the apartment was this noisy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S ことに気がつく means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar may not always be the nominalizer meaning "that." It could be a noun meaning "thing" following the noun-typed usage of this grammar.
急[いそ]いでいたので タクシーに 乗[の]ったら、 道[みち]が 混[こ]んでいて、 かえって 遅[おそ]くなってしまった。
I took a taxi because I was in a hurry, but the roads were crowded and I ended up even later (than I would've been otherwise).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かえって "on the contrary; rather"
メールを 出[だ]すか、 あるいは、 電話[でんわ]を するか、 どちらでも いいが、 とにかく 連絡[れんらく] しなくては いけない。
You may either send an e-mail or call me. Either way is fine, but you must contact me somehow.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1 か、あるいは、S２ か "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
友達[ともだち]が 迎[むか]えに 来[き]たら、 私[わたし]は 帰[かえ]ります。
If/when my friend comes to pick me up, I will leave.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1たらS２。 When たら is used, as opposed to (の)なら, S1 must be completed before S2. 説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
ピクニックの 途中[とちゅう]で、 急[きゅう]に 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]り出[だ]した。
In the middle of the picnic it suddenly started to rain.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu 出す Means: V out; begin to V; start to V; begin V-ing; start V-ing V出す differs from V始める in that V出す is used for abrupt and non-volitional actions, while V始める is used for both volitional and non-volitional actions but NOT for actions which begin abruptly. V-masu 出す has 2 meanings, here is the (2) Someone begins something or something begins
雪[ゆき]さえ 降[ふ]らなければ、 車[くるま]の 運転[うんてん]は 怖[こわ]くない。
As long as it doesn't snow, driving a car isn't scary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
また 朝[あさ] 寝坊[ねぼう] してしまって、 また 授業[じゅぎょう]に 遅[おく]れた。
I overslept again, and again I was late for class.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: In addition to the meaning "again," また expresses the meaning "also" or "additionally." --- 英訳 [English translation]: also; as well; additionally; in addition; moreover --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ また、S。
皆[みな]に 聞[き]こえる ように、 大[おお]きい 声[こえ]で 話[はな]して下[くだ]さい。
Please talk in a loud voice so that everyone can hear you.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
真[ま]っ赤[か]な 夕日[ゆうひ]が 海[うみ]に 沈[しず]んで (to set) いく。
The evening sun, brilliant red, is sinking into the sea.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

真っX where X = adjective or Noun Means: very; pure; totally; right; mid- 真っAdj indicates the degree of something is very high or is at the highest level. 真っNoun indicates the center of a space or time span. The english translation of 真っ varies according to the word that follows it.
先月[せんげつ]は 忙[いそが]しくて、 たった 二日[ふつか]しか、 休[やす]めなかった。
Last month was busy; I could take only two days off.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
たった（の）Number (+counter) "only" This is used to emphasize the small amount or number of something.
私[わたし]は 友達[ともだち]に 「ノートを 見[み]せて下[くだ]さい」と 頼[たの]みました。
Please let me see your notes, I asked of my friend. (Direct Quote)
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように頼む/言う is used to quote a request or command indirectly. In an affirmative request ように頼む is often used with てくれる, as in 来てくれるように頼む. (cf. negative request: ~ないように頼む --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~(てくれる)ように頼む = to ask someone to V ~ように言う = to tell someone to V --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. V-non-plast.plain ように頼む/言う b. V-te くれるように頼む c. V-nai ないように頼む/言う
その 子[こ]は 水[みず]に 飛[と]び込[こ]む 気持[きも]ちには どう しても なれなかった。
He could not bring himself to jump into the water.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 込む "in; into; deeply; heavily; thoroughly; completely" The compound verb base 込む can mean one of 4 things: (B) getting into something {飛び込む}
小[ちい]さい 猫[ねこ]の 声[こえ]は、 赤[あか]ちゃんが 泣[な]いている ように 聞[き]こえます。
The voice of a small cat sounds like a crying baby.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように is used when (1) X resembles Y, (2) when X is as Y shows, says, explains, etc. or (3) when X does something as shown/said/explained, etc. in/by Y. --- 英訳 [English translation]: like; as; as if --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N のように V-plain ように
昨日[きのう]は、 ４[よ]時間[じかん]しか 寝[ね]られなかったので、 眠[ねむ]くて しようが ない。
I only got four hours of sleep yesterday, so I'm very sleepy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-te しようがない "cannot help V-ing; cannot stop feeling ~; so ~; unbearably ~" てしかたない、てしようがない,etc. literally mean that a situation is such or is occurring and there is no way to escape it. The phrases are used to indicate that the speaker is unable to control his psychological/physiological reactions or bear a sensation or an external situation. しかたがない and しようがない are interchangeable. This use is different from the following example, where the しかたがない means "it cannot be helped; there's nothing one can do." お金がないのだから、留学できないのはしかたがない。
やまない 雨[あめ]は ないんですよ。 落[お]ち込[こ]んでいないで 元気[げんき]を 出[だ]しましょう。
All storms (lit. rain) eventually cease. Don't be depressed. Cheer up.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−nai ない N は{ない／いない} Means: There is no N which/who does not V This construction is used to create sentences containing double negatives. VないNは(い)ない is equivalent to "All Ns V."
こんなに たくさんの 人[ひと]が 読[よ]んでいるのだから、 面白[おもしろ]い 本[ほん]であるに 違[ちが]い ない。
With this many people reading it, it must be an interesting book.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜である/~ではない is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
絶対[ぜったい]に 怒[おこ]らない 人[ひと]が いるのだろうか。 私[わたし]は 絶対[ぜったい]に そんな 人[ひと]は いないと 思[おも]う。
I wonder if there really are people who never get mad. I definitely don't think they exist.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.
ルームメートは、 毎日[まいにち] 寝[ね]てばっかり いる。 授業[じゅぎょう]に 行[い]かなくても いいのかなあ。
My roommate does nothing but sleep everyday. I wonder if he doesn't have to go to his lessons.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−te ばかりいる。 Means: Nothing But; always; all the time ばかり is used to express the idea that someone does one thing all the time and does nothing else, or that someone chooses just one thing among others when doing something. Ex: 田中さんはマンガばかり読んでいる。 can mean: (= All tanaka does is read comics); (= Tanaka reads only comics); (=When Masao reads, he reads nothing but comics) NOTE: ばっかり is more colloquial than ばかり
キッチンから 流[なが]れてくる においから すると、 今日[きょう]の 晩御飯[ばんごはん]は カレー ライスかなあ。
The smell from the kitchen makes me think we're having curry tonight.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.
動物[どうぶつ]園[えん]で パンダの 赤[あか]ちゃんが ３[さん]匹[びき] 生[う]まれた そうだ。 こう いう ニュースは うれしい。
I hear that three baby pandas were born at the zoo. This kind of news makes me happy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
今[いま]、 ちょっと 忙[いそが]しくて、 電話[でんわ]で 話[はな]してられないから、 後[あと]で 私[わたし]から かけなおしても いい？
I'm a little busy right now, so I can't talk on the phone any longer. Can I call you back later?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu 直す "again, re-V" 直す, when attached to the masu-stems of verbs, creates compound verbs with the meaning "again; re-."
日本[にほん]語[ご]には 「いらっしゃいます」や 「召[め]し上[あ]がります」など、 いろいろな 敬語[けいご]が ある。
In Japanese, there are various honorific expressions, like irasshaimasu and meshiagarimasu.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
作文[さくぶん]を 書[か]いた ことは 書[か]いたけれど、 まだ 間違[まちが]いが たくさん あるから 書[か]き直[なお]さなくては いけない。
I have written my composition, but there are still lots of errors and I need to do a rewrite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A} - plain.aff ことは {V/A}-plain.aff (が／けれど） "It is certainly true that~, but; indeed ~, but; do V ~, but; ~ is/are/was/etc. ~, but" This structure is used when the speaker/writer admits that the proposition is true but wants to qualify the proposition with an additional remark.
環境[かんきょう] 問題[もんだい]に おいては、 まず、 どう すれば ごみを 減[へ]らす ことが できるかと いう 点[てん]を 問題[もんだい]に すべきだ。
With respect to environmental problems, we should first address the issue of how to reduce the amount of garbage.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N/NP が問題に {される／なる} "X becomes an issue; X is brought up as an issue; X is questioned; X is called into question." X を 問題にする means "to bring X up as an issue" or "to question X." This phrase is often used in the passive form Xが問題にされる. Xが問題になる is also common. The meaning is the same as that of the passive version.
日本[にほん]の 環境[かんきょう]省[しょう]は アメリカの Environmental Protection Agency に 当[あ]たる。
The Japanese かんきょうしょう is equivalent to the American EPA.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

XはYに当たる。 X&Y = Nouns Means: X corresponds to Y; X is equivalent to Y; X is equal to Y This grammar is often used to contrast words/phrases in two languages or organizations/professional titles in two countries.
もう すぐ クリスマスです。 そこで、 日本[にほん]の ホスト ファミリーに 何[なに]か プレゼントを 贈[おく]りたいと 思[おも]っているのですが、 どんな ものを 送[おく]ったらいいでしょうか。
It'll be Christmas pretty soon, so I'd like to send my host family in Japan some kind of present. What do you think I should send?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1, そこで, S2. "Because of that; therefore; so" そこで is used to indicate and action (to be) taken because of the situation presented in S1. それで may replace そこで そこで may only replace それで when S2 is a controllable action. ex. 寒かった。それで、見に来た人が少なかった。 only それで can be used here.
日本[にほん]の 夏[なつ]は とても 暑[あつ]い。 それに 湿度[しつど]も 高[たか]い。
Japan's summers are very sultry. Furthermore, the humidity is also high.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
橋[はし]の 上[うえ]から 真下[ました]に ある 川[かわ]を 見[み]ると、 とても 怖[こわ]い。
From the bridge, if you look straight down at the river, it's really scary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

真っX where X = adjective or Noun Means: very; pure; totally; right; mid- 真っAdj indicates the degree of something is very high or is at the highest level. 真っNoun indicates the center of a space or time span. The english translation of 真っ varies according to the word that follows it.
仕事[しごと]が 忙[いそが]しくても、 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]だけは 食[た]べて下[くだ]さいね。
Even if you are busy at work, at least eat lunch, OK?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When the particle は follows a quantifier (i.e., a word such as 3本 or 少し), it adds the meaning "at least." だけは and ぐらいは (or くらいは) after a noun have the same meaning. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at least. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) は b. N だけは c. N {ぐらい/くらい}は
コンピュータの 知識[ちしき]に 関[かん]しては、 彼[かれ]が 一番[いちばん]だと 思[おも]う。
When it comes to knowledge about computers, I think he's the best.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N に関して は S formal "with regard to; concerning; regarding; about; on; related to" について is similar in meaning to に関して, but is less formal and is used in both written and spoken language.
私[わたし]は 彼[かれ]の ことが 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]の 時[とき]から ずっと 好[す]きだったんです。
I've liked him ever since elementary school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ずっと "all the time; all along; all the way; all through ~; throughout~; ever (since); never (since)" ずっと means that a state or action is ongoing, from one point in time to another point in time (often the moment of speech)
彼女[かのじょ]は 私[わたし]の 母[はは]の 姉[あね]の 娘[むすめ]ですから、 私[わたし]の いとこに 当[あ]たります。
She's my mother's older sister's daughter, so that makes her my cousin.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

XはYに当たる。 X&Y = Nouns Means: X corresponds to Y; X is equivalent to Y; X is equal to Y This grammar is often used to contrast words/phrases in two languages or organizations/professional titles in two countries.
試験[しけん]が 終[お]わってから、 答[こた]えを 間違[まちが]えた ことに 気[き]が つきました。
After the test was over, I realized I had written the wrong answer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S ことに気がつく means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar may not always be the nominalizer meaning "that." It could be a noun meaning "thing" following the noun-typed usage of this grammar.
火事[かじ]や 地震[じしん]の 場合[ばあい]には、 エレベーターを 使[つか]わないでください。
In the event of a fire or an earthquake, please refrain from using the elevator.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
アルバイトで 忙[いそが]しいと いう 理由[りゆう]で、 学校[がっこう]を 休[やす]む 学生[がくせい]が います。
There are students who skip school because they're too busy with their part-time jobs.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.
彼[かれ]は この 大学[だいがく]の 有名[ゆうめい]人[じん]だ。 ほとんどの 人[ひと]が 彼[かれ]の ことを 知[し]っている。
He's famous at his school. Almost everyone knows him.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんどの N means Almost all N; most of N
彼[かれ]が 住[す]みたがっているのは 関東[かんとう]だが、 私[わたし]が 住[す]みたいのは 関西[かんさい]の 方[ほう]だ。
Where he wants to live is Kanto, but Kansai is where I want to live.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: The structure SのはXの方だ is used to emphasize that it is X that makes the proposition in S true. --- 英訳 [English translation]: It is X that S --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ SのはXの方だ。
一緒[いっしょ]に 住[す]んでくれる ルームメートさえ 見付[みつ]かれば、 いつでも 引[ひ]っ越[こ]せる。
If I could just find a roommate to live with, I could move any time.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
私[わたし]の 彼女[かのじょ]が 好[す]きなら、 付[つ]き合[あ]ってくれる ように 頼[たの]んでみたら どうですか。
If you like her, why don't you just ask her if she'll go out with you?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
彼[かれ]らが 言[い]っている ことは よく 分[わ]からない。 私[わたし]たちの 考[かんが]えに 反対[はんたい]なのだろうか。
I don't really understand what they're saying. I wonder if they are disagreeing with our idea.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Personal pronoun ら "these; those; they; -s; and others" [plural dem. pronouns can be used in polite speech] The plural marker ら is often used with demonstrative pronouns and certain personal pronouns. plural personal pronouns are not used in polite speech.
この サイトでは、 iPodの ユーザー同士[どうし]が 意見[いけん]を 交換[こうかん] し合[あ]う ことが できます。
At this site, iPod users can exchange opinions with each other.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N同士 {が／で／を} Indicates that Ns do something together, that Ns do something to/for/against each other, or that someone puts Ns together in some way.
フィンランド語[ご]とか トルコ語[ご]とか、 皆[みな]が 余[あま]り 勉強[べんきょう] してない 言葉[ことば]を 勉強[べんきょう] してみたい。
I want to try studying a language not many people learn, like Finnish or Turkish.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: とか is used to list examples non-exhaustively. It is similar to や in meaning when the examples listed are nouns. Unlike や, however, とか can be preceeded by verb phrases. When two or more items are listed, とか after the final item is optional when it is followed by a particle and mandatory otherwise (like in this example). (Note that や does not occur after the final item). In Subject とか Subject とかする, the final とか is not optional. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/places/etc. like ~; and; or --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun とか Noun (とか) b. Sentence-plain とか Sentence-plain とか {する/できる}
「聞[き]くは 一時[いちじ]の 恥[はじ]、 聞[き]かぬは、 一生[いっしょう]の 恥[はじ]」ですよ。だから、 どんどん 質問[しつもん] してください。
You know what they say: "Asking a question makes for momentary embarrassment; not asking makes for a lifetime of shame." Ask as many questions as you like.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-nai ぬ "not" ぬ is a verb ending from classical Japanese and is equivalent to ない in meaning and form. In modern Japanese, it often appears in set phrases.
この お菓子[かし]は、 冷[つめ]たい まま 食[た]べるより、 電子[でんし] レンジで 温[あたた]めた 方[ほう]が おいしく 食[た]べられますよ。
This sweet is better when you warm it up in the microwave instead of just eating it as it is.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Aまま（で）V "V with ~; V while ~; V as (it is); V without ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の せいで、 グリーンランドの 氷[こおり]が どんどん 溶[と]けて (to melt) いる そうだ。
I heard that due to global warming the ice around Greenland is melting at a fast pace.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

どんどん-V "at a fast pace; one after another; keep V-ing vigorously; with no hesitation; with no delay" どんどん expresses the idea that something proceeds from one stage to the next or continues to happen at a fast pace with no delay, or that someone keeps doing something with no hesitation. In some situations both ますますand どんどん can be used, bearing in mind that ますます does not convey the idea that something happens at a fast pace and cannot describe a controllable future action.
来月[らいげつ] 山田[やまだ] 先生[せんせい]が 結婚[けっこん] するらしいですよ。
It seems that professor Yamada is getting married next month.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜らしい。 Means: seem; apparently; I heard that ~; it looks like The auxiliary i-adjective らしい is used to express the speaker's conjecture based on what he/she has learned through an information source or his/her own observation
勉強[べんきょう]が 忙[いそが]しい ため、 友達[ともだち]と 合[あ]う 時間[じかん]が ない。
I'm busy with my studies, so I don't have time to meet with my friends.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by an i-adjective or a na-adjective or the past form of a verb, it indicates reason or cause. When it is preceded by the non-past form of a verb or a noun, it means either reason/cause or purpose. The meaning is determined from the context. Whenため(に) means reason/cause, it can be replaced by 〜から or 〜ので, which are less formal than 〜ために. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because; due to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {この/その/あの}ため(に)
私[わたし]の 家族[かぞく]は、 父[ちち]を はじめ みんな 辛[つら]い 物[もの]が 大好[だいす]きだ。
In my family, everyone loves spicy food, including my dad.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun をはじめ is used to present a primary example when mentioning a group of things or people. --- 英訳 [English translation]: beginning with~; starting with ~; including ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをはじめ
この 映画[えいが]、 面白[おもしろ] そうなんだけど、 一緒[いっしょ]に 見[み]に 行[い]かない？
This movie looks interesting. Do you want to go see it with me?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}
両親[りょうしん]は 20[にじゅう]年[ねん] 前[まえ]、 つまり、 私[わたし]の 生[う]まれた 年[とし]に 結婚[けっこん] した。
My parents got married 20 years ago - that is, in the year that I was born.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1/NP1, つまり、N2/NP2 "That is (to say); in other words; namely; (that) means; you mean ~?" つまりis used to rephrase or restate what has just been mentioned or stated.
彼[かれ]は ２０[にじゅう]代[だい]で 会社[かいしゃ]を 作[つく]り、 ３０[さんじゅう]代[だい]で、 大[おお]金持[かねも]ちに なった。
He started his company in his twenties and became a very rich man in his thirties.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
10/20/30/etc. ＋ 代 "one's teens/twenties/ thirties/etc." The suffix 代 is used with ten or its multiples to describe someone's approximate age.
もし 時間[じかん]が あったら、 明日[あした] 空港[くうこう]に 迎[むか]えに 来[き]てもらえない？
If you have time, could you come and get me at the airport tomorrow?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
子供[こども]には、 子供[こども]の 年齢[ねんれい]に 合[あ]った 本[ほん]を 与[あた]えた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
You should give children books that are suitable for their age.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 に会った N2 "N2 suitable for N1"
朝寝[あさね]坊[ぼう]を しない ように、 目覚[めざ]まし 時計[とけい]を セット して置[お]きます。
So that I don't sleep in in the morning, I'll set my alarm clock (in preparation).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように
多[おお]くの 国[くに]と 違[ちが]って、 日本[にほん]では ２０歳[はたち]に ならないと 投票[とうひょう] できない。
Unlike most countries, you can't vote in Japan until you turn twenty.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The comparison phrases と同じで and と違って mean "just like ~" and "unlike ~", respectively. Note that the particle と is used when X and Y are in a reciprocal relationship --- 英訳 [English translation]: N と同じで = just like N N と違って = unlike N; different from N --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N と{同じ/違って}
子供[こども]は 5[ご]歳[さい]ぐらいに なれば、 一人[ひとり]で 結構[けっこう] 何[なん]でも できる ようになる。
By the time children become around five years old, they can do quite a bit by themselves.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
結構 (A/ANa +だ) Means: fairly; pretty; rather; quite The adverb 結構 indicates that the speaker feels that the degree/level/amount/etc. of something is not high, but is higher than average
彼[かれ]は 小学[しょうがく]生[せい]だけれど、 かなり 背[せ]が 高[たか]いなあ。 中学[ちゅうがく]生[せい]だと 思[おも]ったよ。
He's an elementary school boy, but he's pretty tall. I thought he was a middle schooler.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
赤[あか]ちゃんが 朝[あさ]まで 泣[な]き続[つづ]けたので、 お母[かあ]さんは 全然[ぜんぜん] 寝[ね]られなかった。
The baby kept crying until morning, so its mother got no sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 続く Means: continue to; continue V-ing; go on V-ing; keep (on) V-ing;all the way; all the time This phrase is used when the subject continues doing something volitionally.
自分[じぶん]は 絶対[ぜったい]に 正[ただ]しいと 思[おも]い込[こ]んでいる 人[ひと]とは、 あまり はなしたくない。
I don't really want to talk to people who are convinced that they are always right.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 込む "in; into; deeply; heavily; thoroughly; completely" The compound verb base 込む can mean one of 4 things: (D) doing something thoroughly and completely {思い込む}
私[わたし]と 両親[りょうしん]の 教[おし]えは いつも 逆[ぎゃく]だ。 どう して こんなに 意見[いけん]が 違[ちが]うのだろう。
My ideas and my parents, ideas are always opposite. Why do we have such different opinions on things?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

X は 逆 だ。 "be opposite; the other way" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
あの 殺人[さつじん] 事件[じけん]から もう 5[ご]年[ねん]も たっているのに、 未[いま]だに 犯人[はんにん]は 捕[つか]まっていない。
It's been five years since that murder (case), but the killer still hasn't been caught.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
今月[こんげつ]の 家賃[やちん]を 払[はら]った はずなのに、 大家[おおや]さんに まだ もらっていないと 言[い]われた。 変[へん]だなあ。
I know I already paid my rent for this month, but my landlord told me he hasn't gotten it yet. How weird.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A} -plain はず [seen here] ANa {な/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった) N {の/じゃない/だった/じゃなかった} "Should; I expect that ~; I believe that~" The dependent noun はず indicates that the speaker/writer or someone he/she empathizes with believes or expects that what is stated before はず is true based on his/her knowledge or memory at the moment of speech or at the time of the event stated in the main clause. The negative form can be either 〜ないはずだ or 〜はずがない.However, the sense of negation is stronger in はずがない. When Sはずだ modifies a noun, の must be used between はず and the noun.
私[わたし]に とって 一番[いちばん] 大切[たいせつ]な ものは 私[わたし]の 猫[ねこ]だが、 猫[ねこ]に とって 一番[いちばん] 大切[たいせつ]な ものは 食[た]べ物[もの]の ようだ。
My cat is the most important thing in the world to me, but for my cat it seems like the most important thing in the world is food.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Xにとって means "to X; for X" in a context where something (or someone) is important to X, or is necessary, useful, good, difficult, etc. for X. X is often a person, a geographic unit or an organization. --- 英訳 [English translation]: for, to, from the standpoint of, as far as ... is concerned --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nに取って
授業[じゅぎょう]を 休[やす]む ときは 先生[せんせい]に 連絡[れんらく] しなくては いけない ことに なっているが、 忘[わす]れてしまった。
We're supposed to let the teacher know if we're going to miss a class, but I forgot.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-past ことになっている means that something has been decided and the result of the decision is still in effect. It is often used to introduce rules or customs, as well as one's schedule. --- 英訳 [English translation]: be supposed to ~; It is a rule that ~; It's been decided that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past ことになっている: {行く/行かない}ことになっている
日本[にほん]に 住[す]んでいた 時[とき]は 地震[じしん]が 少[すく]なくなかったから、 本[ほん]高[こう]の そばに はねない ようにしていた。
There were more than a few earthquakes when I was living in Japan, so I made sure not to sleep near the bookshelf.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {は／が／も} 少なくない "many; much; plenty of; not a few' 少なくない is a double negative meaning "many; much" and is commonly used in written language. It cannot modify nouns. For ex. 少なくない人 is a BAD expression.
私[わたし]は 10[じゅう]台[だい]で 結婚[けっこん] して すぐ 子供[こども]を 産[う]み、 40[よんじゅう]台[だい]で 孫[まご]が 産[う]まれ 「 おばあさん」に なりました。
I got married in my teens and had a child right away, and in my forties my first grandchild was born and I became a grandma.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
10/20/30/etc. ＋ 代 "one's teens/twenties/ thirties/etc." The suffix 代 is used with ten or its multiples to describe someone's approximate age.
エコカーは 空気[くうき]を 汚[よご]さず、 ガソリン代[だい]も あまり かからない ことから、 環境[かんきょう]に やさしい 車[くるま]だと 言[い]える。
Because eco card don't pollute the air and they keep people from spending a lot of money on gas, you could say that they are environment-friendly.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ことから "because; from the fact that" ことから is used to express a reason
この 車[くるま]は ガソリンが なくても 走[はし]れると いう 点[てん]で 環境[かんきょう] (environment) に いいですが、 値段[ねだん]が 高[たか]いです。
This car is good to the environment in that it doesn't need gasoline to run, but it is expensive.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S + という点で "in that ~" 点 is used to mean "point" (in the sense of a single, fact, idea or opinion in an argument, discussion, etc.), "aspect," or "viewpoint/standpoint."
アメリカ的[てき]； 歴史[れきし]的[てき]な 文学[ぶんがく]的[てき]な； 国際[こくさい]的[てき] 一般[いっぱん]的[てき]；
American; historical literary; international general
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N+的 the suffix is attached to nouns to make them な-adjectives. When these adj modify nouns, the な is sometimes omitted.
毎日[まいにち] 寝[ね]る 前[まえ]に、 新[あたら]しい 漢字[かんじ]を 五つ[いつつ] 覚[おぼ]える ようにしています。
I'm trying to learn five new kanji before going to bed every night.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Here one makes an effort at every opportunity to do something to the degree that he or she can, but sometimes fails. Thus ようにする is often used for habitual actions. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする
東京[とうきょう]に 来[く]る 場合[ばあい]は、 連絡[れんらく] してください。 会[あ]いに 行[い]きますから。
If you ever come to Tokyo, let me know. I'll come and see you.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
授業[じゅぎょう]料[りょう]を 幾[いく]ら 払[はら]わなくては 行[い]けないかは、 大学[だいがく]に よって 違[ちが]う。
How much tuition fee you have to pay differs depending on the university.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
今日[きょう]は 忙[いそが]しいけど、 来週[らいしゅう]の 日曜[にちよう] 日[び]で よければ、 一緒[いっしょ]に 行[い]けるよ。
Today I'm busy, but if next sunday is all right we can go together.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N でよければ Means: if ~ is all right; if ~ works; if ~ is acceptable; if you don't mind it presents a condition for doing something. it is also used when the speaker politely offers something to the hearer.
健康[けんこう]の ためには、 毎日[まいにち] 6[ろく]時間[じかん] 以上[いじょう] 寝[ね]る ようにした ほうが いい そうだ。
I've heard that to be healthy, it's best to get six hours or more of sleep every day.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: X以上 and X以下 means "equal to or more than X" and "(equal to or) less than X," respectively. A Number + Counter or a demonstrative pronoun such as これ and それ commonly occurs before 以上 and 以下. When the topic is academic grades, grade symbols such as C and B can be used (e.g., C以上). --- 英訳 [English translation]: 以上 = or more 以下 = less than; or less --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) 以上/以下: ３年生以上 b. Demonstrative pronoun 以上/以下: これ以上; それ以下
地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]に よって 北極[ほっきょく]の 氷[こおり]が 溶[と]けて (to melt) いるらしい。
I've heard that, as an effect of global warming, the ice in the Arctic is melting.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
~ことによって によって indicates the cause, the means, or the agent in passive sentences. In this sentence it indicates CAUSE. "because; because of; due to; by V-ing; by means of; via; through; by"
人[ひと]は 失敗[しっぱい] して 初[はじ]めて、 自分[じぶん]の した ことが 間違[まちが]えていた ことに 気[き]が つく。
It's when people fail that they first realize that what they'd done was wrong.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N に気がつく。 Means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar will not always be the nominalizer meaning "thing." It could be the Sこと form for statements using this grammar.
アメリカでは、 お酒[さけ]が 飲[の]める 年齢[ねんれい]に ついての 規制[きせい]は、 各州[かくしゅう]で それぞれ 違[ちが]う。
In the United States, the rules concerning the legal drinking age are different in each state.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
各 + N "each ~; various" A prefix which adds the meaning "each; various." When the referent of the noun after 各 is unknown, it means "various."
一人[ひとり]で するのが 大変[たいへん]な 場合[ばあい]は、 クラスメートと 一緒[いっしょ]に 宿題[しゅくだい]を しても いいです。
If it's too difficult to do alone, it's all right to work on your homework with your classmates.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
